item.title: Nigeria’s electricity crisis to persist as FG shifts debt payment to 2027
item.description: •Poor teamwork, illiquidity, others undermine efficiency – Tegbe •Power crisis requires structural overhaul – Iledare By Ediri Ejoh Nigeria’s electricity crisis is unlikely to be resolved in 2026, as the Federal Government has shifted the settlement of its N3.3 trillion debt to power generation companies to 2027, while major interventions in metering and transmission infrastructure are also expected to extend beyond this year. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this during an interview with Arise News yesterday, adding that the government had paid N1.23 trillion of the debt, negotiated down from an initial N6 trillion, and was exploring options to clear the outstanding balance. These include offsetting obligations against royalties and corporate income tax, as well as engaging the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPC, to reduce gas costs for power generation companies. “We’re on track to finish paying the rest next year. Because we are looking at different ways to settle it,” Tegbe said. On the proposed debt offsets, he said: “You can’t take money with one hand and give it with the other hand. So, let’s net it off.” Tegbe attributed 80 per cent of the sector’s challenges to human and institutional factors, with technical issues accounting for the remaining 20 per cent. “I said the problem in power sector is 20 per cent technical, 80 per cent human,” he said, identifying poor teamwork, lack of coordination among operators, liquidity constraints and governance issues as major obstacles to efficiency. He also criticised past investment decisions, saying some projects were driven by political considerations rather than proper planning. “From a technical point of view, I will tell you the biggest issue: it is that we’ve been throwing money at wrong things,” he said. The minister said his ministry was reviewing ongoing projects to prioritise investments capable of improving electricity access. Tegbe recently projected that stable electricity supply could take another three to five years. He also announced plans for a $2 billion East-West Super Grid project to expand transmission capacity from about 4,000MW to 19,000MW. The proposed network would link Funtua, Gwagwalada, Ikot Ekpene, Benin, Epe and Ilorin. Procurement is under way, with completion expected within two years, according to the minister. Reacting, Professor Emeritus of Petroleum Economics, Wumi Iledare, called for a structural overhaul, warning that replacing individuals would not resolve the sector’s deep-rooted problems. “Darkness arising from persistent electricity failures in Nigeria is not fundamentally a consequence of individual ineptitude; it is a manifestation of institutional failure,” he said. item.title: Delta attack: Nobody will kill at rallies if law catches up with them — Falana
item.description: Senior Advocate of Nigeria and human rights activist Femi Falana has warned that recurring pre-election violence and political killings will persist unless perpetrators face swift prosecution and legal accountability ahead of the 2027 polls. Speaking on Channels Television ’s Politics Today on Monday, Falana described recent election-related fatalities — including killings reported in Delta State — as tragic and preventable, blaming entrenched impunity across past tragedies and political clashes. He noted that attacks on political figures and convoys are often met with little or no consequence, creating a climate where violent tactics are normalized. “The stakes are high for the political class, but in this unfortunate incident, nothing may come of it. Yesterday, we lost scores of people in Bayelsa State in what was a boat accident. What would happen? Donations have already started; who is the owner of the boat? “Nobody would have thought they were going to kill people in a rally if they know that the law will catch up with them,” Falana said. Falana urged the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), civil society, and other stakeholders to step up rather than leaving political affairs solely to politicians. “Arrests may be made in Delta State, but I am challenging the Nigerian Bar Association and the human rights community to intervene very decisively because if we leave the affairs of our country in the hands of politicians, we will run into a serious crisis,” he said. He further called on the NBA to mobilize lawyers to help the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) prosecute electoral offenders, arguing that INEC is already stretched by pre-election and post-election litigation and lacks the bandwidth to handle prosecutions alone. Beyond electoral violence and credibility concerns — such as voter register cleanup, official accountability, and result transmission — Falana pressed political parties and candidates to campaign on concrete governance issues rather than ethnicity or religion. He pointed to unspent basic education funds at the state level, compulsory health insurance and child rights laws, fuel subsidy controversies, crude-for-loans commitments, and stalled refinery rehabilitations as areas requiring public debate and enforcement. Despite mounting frustrations, Falana rejected the idea that Nigeria is beyond hope, arguing that existing laws can drive change if citizens, the media, and civil society enforce accountability. “So for me it’s not a hopeless situation. item.title: Intrigues, factors shaping battle for 7 North-West states
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo, Haruna Aliyu, Musa Ubandawaki, Idris Salisu, Fauziyya Lawal, Hadiza Yusuf & Muhammad Inuwa THE battle for the seven North-West state government houses of Kaduna, Jigawa, Sokoto, Kano, Kebbi, Katsina and Zamfara is gathering momentum ahead of the February 6, 2027 governorship elections, with incumbent governors seeking fresh mandates amid growing opposition activities, political defections and shifting alliances. Although the All Progressives Congress, APC, controls all the states and enjoys the advantage of incumbency, the emerging political landscape suggests that none of the contests can be taken for granted. The African Democratic Congress, ADC, is positioning itself as a rallying platform for politicians dissatisfied with the ruling party, while the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, is banking on its traditional grassroots structures and political networks. In Kaduna, Governor Uba Sani faces a familiar challenger, Isa Ashiru of the ADC. In Jigawa, Governor Umar Namadi confronts Mustapha Sule Lamido of the PDP and Senator Sabo Muhammad Nakudu of the ADC. Sokoto presents a potentially bruising contest between Governor Ahmed Aliyu and former Deputy Governor Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, while Kano Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf faces opposition candidates and the political consequences of his separation from former political benefactor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. In Kebbi, Governor Nasir Idris faces former Attorney-General of the Federation, Abubakar Malami, who is seeking to capitalise on public dissatisfaction. Katsina Governor Dikko Umaru Radda is challenged by Senators Yakubu Lado Danmarke and Ahmad Babba Kaita of the PDP and ADC respectively. In Zamfara, Governor Dauda Lawal, who defected from the PDP to the APC, faces Senator Kabiru Marafa of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, and other opposition candidates. Across the seven states, insecurity, particularly banditry, kidnapping, attacks on rural communities and displacement, is emerging as a defining electoral issue. Economic hardship, unemployment, poverty and the rising cost of living will also influence voters’ assessment of the incumbents. The governors must contend with internal party rivalries and the challenge of translating government projects and political appointments into votes. The opposition, on its part, must convert public dissatisfaction, endorsements and growing political visibility into effective grassroots mobilisation. item.title: N4.11trn dividend: How 65 firms beat economic crunch
item.description: *81 companies fail to pay *As earnings hit N9.29trn *MTN, Dangote Cement, BUA Foods, GTBank, Zenith, others dominate payout *Shareholders get cash, companies retain N5.18trn for growth *Analysts warn: High dividend payout could constrain expansion if earnings weaken By Peter Egwuatu For thousands of investors who put their money into the Nigerian stock market, the real reward from owning shares is often not the daily movement in stock prices, but the cash that eventually lands in their accounts. That reward amounted to a staggering N4.11 trillion for shareholders of 65companies quoted on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), as the companies paid out the sum as dividends from combined net income of N9.29 trillion in the financial year 2025, amid the ongoing economic reforms of the Federal Government. The dividend payout comes against the backdrop of wide-ranging economic reforms by the Federal Government, including the removal of the petrol subsidy, exchange-rate reforms and measures aimed at improving government revenue, investment and the business environment. Against this backdrop, dividend payments have become particularly significant for investors seeking to preserve returns and generate income amid persistent economic pressures. The dividend declared means that the companies distributed about 44.2 per cent of their combined earnings to shareholders, leaving approximately N5.18 trillion, or 55.8 per cent, within the businesses. For shareholders, the numbers represent a major income stream at a time when investors are increasingly looking for reliable returns from the capital market. Vanguard’s latest findings show that, out of the 146 listed companies, 81 companies did not declare dividends to their shareholders. But behind the dividend bonanza lies a bigger concern for the companies and the Nigerian economy: how much should businesses distribute today and how much should they retain to finance tomorrow’s growth? MTN, Dangote Cemen, BUA Foods lead N4.11trn payout The dividend distribution was heavily driven by some of the country’s biggest and most profitable listed companies. MTN Nigeria topped the table with N860.83 billion in dividend payments, followed by Dangote Cement with N753.80 billion. BUA Foods paid N504 billion, while Guaranty Trust Bank (GTBank) and Zenith Bank paid N429.83 billion and N410.69 billion, respectively. BUA Cement distributed N338.64 billion, while HBM Nigeria paid N257.70 billion. The other three companies that made the top 10 were Aradel Holdings, N99.0 billion; Stanbic IBTC Holdings, N63.61 billion; and Ecobank Transnational Incorporated, N52.80 billion. The scale of the payouts shows the growing importance of large listed companies to investors who depend on dividend income. For a retail investor holding shares directly, the dividend represents cash income. item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32
item.description: •As Bayelsa deploys crane to lift wreckage of capsized boat •PANDEF mourns victims •Police AIG visits Ayama-Ijaw By Samuel Oyadongha & Henry Umoru The death toll in last Friday’s boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 32, as the state government deployed a heavy-duty crane to the scene to lift the wreckage of the capsized vessel and facilitate a thorough search for persons who may still be trapped beneath or within it. This came as Pan Niger Delta Forum, PANDEF, the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, mourned victims of the recent boat accident that claimed several lives. Also, the Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited the Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw to interact with marine workers and the Red Cross rescue team over the fatal boat mishap. The operation, involving the Bayelsa State Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency, BYSEMA, the National Inland Waterways Authority, NIWA, security agencies, divers and other relevant responders, is continuing as the government intensifies efforts to account for all persons affected by the tragic incident. It was learned that the deployment of the crane was aimed at removing the submerged wreckage and enabling divers and rescue personnel to properly examine the site, while extending the search to areas that may not have been accessible during the initial operations. The state government had sustained the search and recovery effort since the mishap, with relevant agencies working to ensure that every part of the affected waterway and the wreckage was thoroughly examined. The latest deployment signals an escalation of the multi-agency operation, as authorities move to conclusively determine the fate of passengers who remain unaccounted for since the vessel went down. The boat tragedy, which occurred on the state’s inland waterways, around Oweikorogha and Otuan junction in the council, has once again brought to the fore concerns over water transportation safety in Bayelsa, a riverine state where boats serve as a primary means of movement for many communities. PANDEF mourns victims In a statement by PANDEF National Chairman, Amb. item.title: Curfew in Delta: How gunmen killed 4 in Omo-Agege’s convoy
item.description: By Henry Umoru No fewer than four persons were killed, yesterday, as gunmen opened fire on members of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, who were on the campaign train of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Omo-Agege is the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the NDC in 2027 National Assembly polls. While the NDC claimed the All Progressives Congress, APC, was responsible for the attack, the ruling party accused the NDC of stoking the attack, which, it alleged, claimed three of its members. But the state police command said it was investigating the attack. Among NDC members killed was Moses Anaughe, a former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission and aide to Omo-Agege. A former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evans Ivwurie, was among those shot and currently battling for his life alongside other victims receiving medical attention. Videos circulating on social media showed Umukoro, popularly known as Akhima, lying motionless at a hospital where efforts were being made to revive him. Another video showed Iwurie being assisted into a hospital, with blood stains visible around his chest. This came as the Delta State government imposed a curfew on Ughelli North, following the gunshots and attendant deaths in parts of the council. Meanwhile, Ughelli North Council Chairman, Olorogun Jaro Egbo, claimed that three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing the each other of instigating the violence. The State Police condemned the killings, and commenced investigations to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The latest bloodshed was the third major violent incident linked to political activities involving rival camps in the state, following earlier clashes in the Warri-Effurun axis and Asaba, where one person was killed. While Omo-Agege’s camp put the Uduere death toll at four, Egbo claimed three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing each other of instigating the violence. The recurrence of deadly confrontations, with the 2027 general elections still months away, has heightened concerns over the safety of political campaigns and the possibility of Delta becoming increasingly engulfed in political violence. Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage at close range during a peaceful campaign visit, describing the incident as an assassination attempt. item.title: Peter Obi lacks capacity to manage people properly — Abure
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party (LP), Julius Abure has accused Peter Obi of lacking the capacity to unite and manage people, citing the departure of several figures who worked with the party’s 2023 presidential candidate. Abure made the allegation on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, while explaining his fallout with Obi and his decision to support President Bola Tinubu. “Peter Obi doesn’t have capacity to manage people properly. I ask you, the structure we built around him in the 2023 general election. Where are the people? Where is Yunusa Tanko? He is in another party. You are looking at me because I’m saying I’m supporting Bola Tinubu. Yunusa Tanko is no longer with Peter,” Abure said. “Ask yourself what happened to Yunusa Tanko. Ask yourself where is Sarah Ibrahim? Where is his vice-presidential candidate in the 2023 general election? Where are a lot of others? Where is people like Valentine Ozigbo? There are many others. The man simply does not have the capacity, the character, and competence to put people together and galvanise them towards achieving a set goal.” Abure denied ever frustrating Obi out of the Labour party, saying the party had given him substantial control after the 2023 election. He argued that Obi’s experience with political parties and the Obidient movement showed, in his view, that he had struggled to keep people together. “There was no frustration, we gave him everything. We practically handed over the leadership of the party to him, and that was the truth of the matter. If you go and find out, you are journalists. I’m sure a lot of your people were with us during the campaign. “After the campaign, I practically almost handed over the party for him to run, and the result is what you have seen,” he said. “Peter Obi himself will tell you: Look at people’s past. Look at Obi’s past. Look at APGA, look at PDP, look at Labour now, and look at the people that are with him, even in the Obidient movement, how they have all abandoned him and left him because he doesn’t have that capacity to put people together and manage them for effective performance.” Abure also said his experience working with Obi, who is now contesting the 2027 election under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), had convinced him that the former Anambra governor was “unstable” and “unreliable.” He said he chose to support Tinubu ahead of the 2027 elections because he believed the president was better suited to lead. “You see, experience they say is the best teacher. item.title: 970m Africans lack access to clean cooking — Energy expert
item.description: By Ediri Ejoh & Henry Obetta About 970 million Africans lack access to clean cooking, while over 560 million people in sub-Saharan Africa are without electricity, energy experts have said, calling for greater continental collaboration to tackle the crisis. Regional Chair for Africa of the World Energy Council, Mr Omar Farouk, disclosed this at the 14th anniversary lecture and investiture into the Realnews Hall of Fame, organised by Realnews Magazine, with the theme: “Geopolitical Turbulence and Energy Security: Forging Strategic Opportunities for Africa.” Citing the 2026 Tracking SDG 7 Report, based on 2024 data, Farouk lamented Africa’s energy poverty despite its abundant oil, gas and renewable resources. “How can a continent so richly endowed with energy resources remain so energy poor? Why do petroleum-producing countries sometimes struggle to supply affordable fuels to their own citizens? Why do countries with natural gas resources suffer from electricity shortages?” he asked. He attributed the crisis largely to inadequate finance, technology and infrastructure, rather than resource scarcity. “We cannot, as a continent, be able to get out of where we have found ourselves today if we continue to operate in silos. Our solution lies in cooperation and collaboration,” he said. Farouk stressed that finance, technology and infrastructure must work together to drive energy development, adding: “You can have a lot of money without the technology, you can’t make any progress. You can bring scientists, technologists, without the money, they can’t make progress. And you can have both of these without the energy infrastructure, you can’t move energy from one point to the other.” He said Africa was projected to attract only $110 billion, or 3.3 per cent of the estimated $3.4 trillion global energy investment in 2026, while universal clean cooking access would require about $4 billion annually. Managing Director of Frazimex Engineering Limited, a subsidiary of Oilserv Group, Engr. Chuka Eze, urged African countries to leverage global geopolitical disruptions to strengthen energy sovereignty and industrial capacity. He said Africa captures less than one per cent of the value generated from clean-energy technology manufacturing, despite its rich mineral resources. “Africa’s opportunity is to move from being a supplier of strategic resources to becoming a shaper of the global energy system,” Eze said. He called for stronger local-content policies, technology transfer, skills development and regional cooperation to promote domestic processing, manufacturing and industrial growth. item.title: Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment. Musa, who spoke at the National Growth & Development Forum (NGDF) 2026 in Abuja, said Nigeria lost the link between economic planning and execution, resulting in the abandonment or underperformance of strategic national projects. “History demands candour. Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain,” he said. According to him, the oil windfall of the 1970s diverted the country from agriculture and non-oil exports which had previously sustained the economy. “The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us. Strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to fulfil it four decades on. “And when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations,” Musa said. He said Nigeria must learn from its past policy failures to avoid repeating mistakes that have undermined economic development. “The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have,” he added. The NES president also expressed concern that economic reforms had yet to translate into shared prosperity, noting that about 63 per cent of Nigerians, estimated at 140 million people, lived below the poverty line in 2025, according to the World Bank. “Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” he said. Musa called for an economy that generates jobs, supports the poor, boosts domestic production, invests in human capital and promotes disciplined public finance and credible institutions. Similarly, President, Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms must be measured by their impact on citizens’ welfare, job creation, purchasing power and poverty reduction. item.title: 2027: ‘As You Do For Me, I Do For You,’ Tinubu Seeks Igbo Support In Lagos
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. President Tinubu made the call while addressing Igbo stakeholders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos, on Monday. ﻿ President Tinubu said that though he was displeased when he lost the 2023 election in the state, which is considered a stronghold of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), the matter had been settled. “Some of you didn’t vote for me in 2023; I vex o . We don settle. Get your PVC,” he urged the crowd. Tinubu also asked if they would vote for him, to which they replied with a resounding “Yes.” After receiving assurance from the stakeholders to back his re-election bid, the president said, “Come January 16, get your PVC; you come vote. Agreement na agreement o, na Bola Tinubu be APC o. As you do for me, I do for you.” ‘Follow Who Know Road’ President Tinubu called for national unity and collective responsibility, urging Nigerians to see themselves as one people with a shared future, in the interest of the country. “You must follow who know road. I have to work hard to make sure the economy improves, to ensure that your children are in school, to eliminate crises in the universities, to build good roads that will maintain our cars. “The future is in our hands. For every one of us, our children must be in school. Because we are poor doesn’t mean they shouldn’t attend the universities,” he added. Tinubu further said the country must rise above its divisions, noting that its development depended on the participation and commitment of all its people. Also speaking, the Governor of Lagos State, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, urged Igbo residents to support Tinubu’s re-election and vote for all candidates of the APC in the 2027 general elections. The governor also implored them to work for the emergence of the Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, as the next Governor of Lagos State. During the meeting, the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; the Minister of State for Budget and Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite; and the former Minister of Labour and Employment, Nkiruka Onyejeocha, as well as other Igbo leaders and stakeholders, assured President Tinubu of their support. The Independent National Electoral Commission said Peter Obi, who was the candidate of the Labour Party, polled 582,454 votes in Lagos, higher than the 572,606 votes polled by Tinubu in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial hub, has one of the highest numbers of registered voters for the 2027 general elections. Emphasising the electoral importance of Lagos, Tinubu described it as a big deal to him. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. item.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. item.title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted. Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for. He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians. Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected. Niger residents gather for an engagement of NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan. The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections. NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes. Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC. Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC. Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027.
